content: 1. Budesonide can reduce the levels or effects of bosentan by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 2. Budesonide and bumetanide may exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing the risk of hypokalemia, especially when budesonide has strong glucocorticoid activity. Close monitoring is recommended. 3. Budesonide can lower the levels or effects of buspirone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution should be exercised, and close monitoring is advised. 4. Butabarbital can decrease the levels or effects of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are necessary. 5. Butalbital can also reduce the levels or effects of budesonide through CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Budesonide decreases calcium acetate levels by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 7. Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 8. The dissolution of extended-release budesonide tablets is pH-dependent. Co-administration with drugs that increase gastric pH may lead to premature dissolution, potentially altering the drug's release properties and absorption in the duodenum. 9. Budesonide decreases calcium carbonate levels by increasing elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 10. Budesonide reduces calcium chloride levels by enhancing elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 11. Budesonide decreases calcium citrate levels by increasing elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 12. Budesonide reduces calcium gluconate levels by enhancing elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 13. Budesonide can lower the levels or effects of carbamazepine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative therapies should be considered. 14. Carbamazepine can reduce the levels or effects of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 15. Budesonide and celecoxib may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, raising the risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 16. Cenobamate can decrease the levels or effects of budesonide by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when co-administered with cenobamate. 17. Ceritinib can increase the levels or effects of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 18. Budesonide can reduce the levels or effects of cevimeline by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 19. Budesonide and chlorothiazide may exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing the risk of hypokalemia, especially with strong glucocorticoid activity. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 20. Budesonide and chlorthalidone may also exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, raising the risk of hypokalemia, particularly with strong glucocorticoid activity. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 21. Cholestyramine decreases budesonide levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Budesonide and choline magnesium trisalicylate may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Budesonide reduces choline magnesium trisalicylate levels by increasing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 24. Budesonide decreases chromium levels by enhancing renal clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 25. Budesonide can lower the levels or effects of cilostazol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Cimetidine reduces the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 27. Cimetidine can increase the levels or effects of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 28. Budesonide can reduce the levels or effects of cinacalcet by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Citric acid/sodium bicarbonate reduces the effects of budesonide by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 30. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 31. Clarithromycin also increases the levels or effects of budesonide by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 32. Budesonide can reduce the levels or effects of clarithromycin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 33. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of clomipramine by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Budesonide reduces the levels or effects of vaginal conjugated estrogens by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Budesonide decreases the levels or effects of cortisone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Crizotinib increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction may be needed for co-administered drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A. 44. Crofelemer increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Crofelemer may inhibit CYP3A4 in the gut but is unlikely to inhibit it systemically due to minimal absorption. 45. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 47. Cyclosporine increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism and inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Dabrafenib decreases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 49. Budesonide and dalteparin may interact, as corticosteroids can decrease anticoagulant effects by increasing blood coagulability or impair vascular integrity, raising bleeding risk. Monitor INR closely. 50. Danazol increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Budesonide and danazol may enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing edema formation. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Danicopan increases budesonide levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Budesonide decreases dapsone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 53. Darifenacin increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Darunavir increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Budesonide reduces darunavir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Dasatinib increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Budesonide reduces dasatinib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Deferasirox decreases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Gastric ulceration and GI bleeding have been reported with deferasirox; use caution when co-administering with drugs that increase the risk of peptic ulcers or gastric hemorrhage, including corticosteroids. 57. Budesonide and denosumab require caution in patients on concomitant immunosuppressants or with impaired immune systems due to an increased risk of serious infections. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Budesonide decreases dexamethasone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Dexlansoprazole reduces budesonide effects by increasing gastric pH, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 60. DHEA (herbal) increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Dichlorphenamide and budesonide both decrease serum potassium. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Budesonide and diclofenac may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism, raising the risk of gastrointestinal ulceration. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Budesonide and diflunisal may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 65. Diltiazem increases budesonide levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use of CYP3A4 inhibitors and oral budesonide. If co-administration is necessary, monitor closely for signs and symptoms of corticosteroid excess. 66. Budesonide decreases the effects of diphtheria and tetanus toxoids by pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is contraindicated. Corticosteroids also increase the risk of infection with concomitant live vaccines. 67.
